class.name: FoliageType
class.brief_description: One kind of grass or object that grows on a [Terrain3D], and the rules for where.
class.description: A foliage type describes what to draw and where it may grow. It does not hold where it has been painted, which lives in [FoliageData], so one type saved as a resource can be used on every terrain in a game. Grass ([constant KIND_GRASS]) is painted as a density and grown procedurally around the camera, drawing its [member mesh] with that mesh's own materials. A grass type with no mesh falls back to simple built-in blades with a wind shader, shaped and coloured by the [code]grass_*[/code] settings, which is enough to block out a level before the real grass is made. Objects ([constant KIND_OBJECT]) are placed one by one and kept: trees, rocks, fences, lamp posts. Give them a [member mesh], optionally with a [member collision_shape], and they are drawn with a [MultiMesh]; or give them a [member scene] and each one is a full instance of it, with its own scripts, lights and collision. Both kinds follow the same placement rules: [member slope_min] and [member slope_max] keep them off cliffs, and [member layer_mask] limits them to where certain layers are painted, so grass only grows where the grass texture is.

method.name: get_render_mesh
method.description: Returns the mesh the type is drawn with: [member mesh], or the built-in grass for a grass type without one.

members.member: How much each instance leans with the slope of the ground, from [code]0.0[/code] for standing straight up, as trees do, to [code]1.0[/code] for following the ground, as rocks and grass do.
If [code]true[/code], the instances cast shadows. Worth leaving off for grass, which has many instances and small shadows.
The collision each object gets, positioned, rotated and scaled with it. Only used by objects drawn from a [member mesh]; a [member scene] brings its own.
How much the brightness of grass varies from blade to blade.
How many grass instances grow per square metre where the density is painted at full strength.
The colour at the roots of the built-in grass.
The number of blades in each tuft of the built-in grass.
The height in metres of the tallest blades of the built-in grass.
The colour at the tips of the built-in grass.
The width in metres of a blade of the built-in grass at its root.
Raises (or, negative, sinks) every instance relative to the ground. Sinking rocks a little hides the gap under them.
Whether this is grass, grown from a painted density, or objects placed one by one.
The terrain layers this may grow on, one bit per layer index. [code]0[/code] means anywhere.
How strongly the layers in [member layer_mask] must be painted, together, for this to grow.
A material to draw the instances with in place of the mesh's own.
The mesh drawn for each instance. A grass type without one draws the built-in grass.
If [code]true[/code], each instance is turned to a random direction.
The most, in degrees, each instance leans off vertical at random, for trees that do not all stand perfectly straight.
The largest random scale an instance gets.
The smallest random scale an instance gets.

For objects, a scene instanced at every placement in place of [member mesh]. Use it for things that need more than a mesh: scripts, lights, sounds, several collision shapes. Heavier than a mesh, so best for dozens or hundreds of objects rather than thousands. The instances are not saved in the scene.
The steepest slope, in degrees, this may grow on.
The gentlest slope, in degrees, this may grow on. Raise it for things that only belong on hillsides.
The closest, in metres, the object brush places two objects of this type to each other.
If [code]true[/code], grass takes on the colour painted on the ground beneath it and darkens where the ground is wet.
How far from the camera, in metres, instances are drawn. Grass is only grown this far out. [code]0.0[/code] draws objects at any distance, and grass to 100 metres.
How much the built-in grass sways in the wind.

constants.constant: Painted as a density and grown around the camera.
